$comment: The values this repository is willing to pass for arguments the inventory cannot give a
domain to, plus the arguments it refuses to vary and why.
Paths point inside the oracle container, where MakeFixtures.java writes the corpus. They are
not committed files: the corpus is rebuilt from the program on every run, which keeps it
deterministic and keeps binary fixtures out of the tree.
Adding a value here widens a covering array. Adding an exclusion narrows it, and the reason
is required, because an exclusion is the one thing in this file that makes a coverage claim

$why: `--INPUT` is one argument name over tools that do not read the same kind of file. The
values above are BAMs and SAMs, which is right for the record transforms and wrong for
everything else: a covering array that hands BedToIntervalList a BAM is a set of rows the
reference refuses for one reason, and it measures the fixture rather than the tool. That is
why the tools below had no array at all.
A tool's own values replace the shared ones for that tool alone (gatk-rs's
tools/coverage/domains.py). Adding one widens the programme by making a tool measurable; it
narrows nothing, because the value it replaces was not a value that tool could take.
The input is another tool's metrics file, so INPUT names the two the corpus writes. They
differ in every counter, which is what makes a row that reads one a different answer from
a row that reads the other. The summing across files is not observable from an array: a
row carries one value per argument, and the tool sums the files it is given several of.
The tag groups are free-form strings with no default, so without them the array cannot run
the tool at all: SEQUENCE_TAG_GROUP is required. Two values, one naming a tag every read
of tagged.bam carries and one naming a pair of them, and the quality groups match. FASTQ
and SECOND_END_FASTQ are the base tool's, and the array compares the TAG file, which is
what this tool adds.
MINIMUM_MQ and MINIMUM_BARCODE_BQ are declared because both have a default and no bounds,
so the generator would hold them there and the array would vary one boolean. The values
straddle what umi.bam carries: mapping qualities of 25 and 60, and a barcode quality of
twenty in the reads that carry a BQ tag at all.
INPUT is a VCF here and a BAM in the shared values, so the tool needs its own; DBSNP is
the sites-only file the corpus writes beside it, every other site of which is in the
input, so the known and novel partitions are both non-empty. Its second value is the
input itself, under which every site is known and the novel partition empties.
TARGET_INTERVALS decides which sites are counted at all, and the two lists cover
different ones, so it is the argument that moves the totals.
HEADER is a required File with no default: the generator gives a path-typed argument no
domain, so without this the tool could not run at all. The header taken is the SAM
fixture's, which shares the corpus's dictionary, so the replacement is a real reheader
rather than a mismatch.
The digest is a function of the header's @RG records and of nothing else, so the three
shared inputs give one answer and the array covers its arguments without testing them.
one_read_group.bam is the same corpus under a single read group, which is the one thing
this tool reads.
RGLB, RGPL, RGPU and RGSM are required Strings with no default, so the generator can give
them no domain and the runner cannot pass them: every row of this tool's array was a
usage error, which measures the argument parser. These four values are what this
repository is willing to pass; they are held constant, so the array covers the arguments
that are actually varied and the tool runs at all.
The shared --INPUT list is BAMs, and this tool reads a FASTA. INTERVALS is optional in the
tool and held by the shared list, so every row takes the masked path; two interval lists
are declared because the count is the only output there is, and one list would make the
array cover the arguments without observing any of them.
The reference is named --REFERENCE here, not --REFERENCE_SEQUENCE, so the shared value
does not reach it and the argument is required: without this every row was a usage error.
MODE's four values are declared here because the pinned inventory does not carry them:
the argument's type is a nested enum named Mode, and the dump left enum_members null for
all seven arguments of that type, so the generator excludes it as an unmodelled type. The
values are the enum's own, in its declaration order.
INPUT is narrowed to two files because the shared ones cannot answer anything: every pair
in them carries the same duplicate flag on both ends, so the tool finds nothing whatever
MODE says. inconsistent_duplicates.bam flips one flag per template, choosing which record
of the pair so that each of the four modes reports a different set of names.
Both sides are the same file, and the two samples are what makes the comparison say
anything: sample1 against sample1 is perfect concordance, sample1 against sample2 is a
real contingency table. CALL_SAMPLE is held at one value so the array varies the truth
side alone, which is enough to reach both shapes.
The numeric arguments are declared here because each has a default and no bounds, so the
generator holds them at that default and the array varies nothing but the booleans. These
are the five that decide something on this corpus: the seed the grouping uses, the quality
floor, the difference rate, the group floor the metrics apply, and the pixel distance the
optical duplicates are found within.
INPUT is complexity.bam, whose pairs actually repeat: on the shared fixtures every group
holds one pair and MIN_GROUP_COUNT drops the lot.
Two inputs that answer the skip check differently: original_quals.bam carries OQ and no
mate cigar, so the tool runs; mate_cigar.bam carries a mate cigar and no OQ, so the tool
returns having written nothing at all. MAX_RECORDS_TO_EXAMINE is left at its default
because the answer is decided by the first informative record either way.
TRIOS is a pedigree file with no default, so the tool cannot run without one declared;
trio.vcf and trio.ped are the corpus. MIN_GQ and MIN_DP are declared because both have a
default and no bounds: the values straddle the child genotype qualities the fixture
carries, so lowering the floor admits a de novo call the default refuses to judge.
The input is a haplotype database, which no shared value provides, and CHAIN has no
default. haplotypes.txt carries two SNPs past chr1:1500, where lift.chain covers nothing,
so every row of this array is the partial answer AND the 101 exit code the tool reports
for it.
CHAIN has no default and the tool cannot run without one, so the corpus writes lift.chain:
it moves the first thousand bases of chr1 five hundred to the right, maps the first five
hundred of chr2 onto themselves, and covers nothing else. MIN_LIFTOVER_PCT is declared
because the second interval of targets.interval_list is covered by a third of its length:
at the default it is rejected and at 0.3 it lifts, which is a different file AND a
different exit code.
Three coordinate-sorted BAMs with different contents, so the index is an answer rather than a
constant; a SAM text file, which the tool refuses by type; and a queryname-sorted and an
unsorted BAM, which it refuses by the header's SO before it reads a record.
Two BAMs of different sort orders, which the tool copies alike, and a SAM file it refuses by
name. COMMENT is required and holds one comment per row; the values carry no space because
the oracle's command line is split by a shell.
Two BAMs, which take the block-copying path, and a SAM, which takes gatherNormally and is
written as a BAM, because makeWriter writes SAM text only for a .sam name. One input per row:
INPUT is a list, and the array holds one of its values per row.
Paired BAMs of different contents and sort orders, and the SAM form of small.bam.
MINIMUM_PCT reaches both of its effects: 0.5 discards every orientation that holds less than
half the pairs, which on a single-orientation input still writes, and 0.6 is refused by the
tool's own validation. HISTOGRAM_WIDTH and MIN_HISTOGRAM_WIDTH trim and widen the histogram,
STOP_AFTER cuts the walk short. METRIC_ACCUMULATION_LEVEL is held at ALL_READS, its default:
the other levels are the port's limitation.
HISTOGRAM_WIDTH is 300 rather than a width that trims every insert away: that makes R fail on a
file with no histogram, and the log line it fails with carries the second it ran at.
The two files are positional, so they are held: small.bam against inconsistent_duplicates.bam,
which agree on every mapping and differ on sixty-three duplicate marks, so the verdict is the
exit code one with the file written. LENIENT_HEADER and LENIENT_DUP are held at false: they
are the port's limitation. The OUTPUT is optional and named, so the rows compare the file.
INPUT is a VCF, and the two orders of the same samples are two answers: in a file whose
sample names are sorted the codec keeps each genotype block lazy, and a block that is never
decoded is copied, while in the other it is decoded and re-encoded. The file without contig
lines is what CREATE_INDEX refuses. SAMPLE is the set of samples kept: `null` clears it to
the default empty set (a sites-only file), sampleA keeps one column, and sampleZ names a
sample the file does not have, which the writer still gives a column of no-calls. OUTPUT
ends in .vcf because the writer infers its format from the extension and refuses output.txt.
The tool accepts at most one sample, so INPUT is two one-sample files (sampleA, hand-written
so its genotype blocks are not htsjdk's own encoding, and sample1, written by htsjdk), the
sites-only file (no sample, which is accepted until OLD_SAMPLE_NAME asks for the first one),
and the two-sample file it refuses. OLD_SAMPLE_NAME is `null` (not checked) or sampleA, which
one input has and the other is refused for, naming the sample found. OUTPUT ends in .vcf for
the reason MakeSitesOnlyVcf's does.
INPUT is a VCF. The hand-written one has filtered sites, overlapping and abutting sites,
IDs on some and not others, and a symbolic deletion with an END, so INCLUDE_FILTERED and
VARIANT_ID_METHOD both change the file; variants.vcf is the htsjdk-written one, and the
file without contig lines has no dictionary for the output header, which is a refusal.
INPUT is a VCF whose records are out of order on two contigs, under both sample orders
(the output header's samples are the SORTED names, so the second is rewritten column by
column), plus the file without contig lines, which needs SEQUENCE_DICTIONARY. That argument
is `null`, the corpus's own dictionary (which agrees with the VCFs), and other.dict, which
does not and is refused. It is read through SamReaderFactory, so it is a .dict, not the
FASTA the shared value names. INPUT is one file per row: a second input would need two
values in one row, which the harness cannot pass.
INPUT is a VCF under both sample orders, plus the one with no contig lines to replace.
SEQUENCE_DICTIONARY goes through SAMSequenceDictionaryExtractor, which picks a reader by
extension: the FASTA (whose .dict beside it is read), a .dict that disagrees with the
corpus and carries an assembly, a VCF's contig lines, an interval list's header, and a VCF
with no contig lines, whose dictionary is null: refused by the writer when it is to index
and by setSequenceDictionary when it is not.
INPUT and COMMENT are whole lists ($lists): what MergeVcfs does is combine several inputs, and
a row with one of them measures a copy. merge_a.vcf and merge_b.vcf are each in coordinate
order and meet at three positions, where MergingIterator's heap (not the input order) decides
which record comes first; b's samples are in the other column order, so its genotypes are
re-encoded while a's are copied, and its XC line promotes a's count to `.`. The pair is given
both ways round, and a alone. merge_b_no_contigs.vcf needs SEQUENCE_DICTIONARY (ref.dict makes
it compatible, other.dict adds chr3 and is refused), and as the FIRST input it takes that
dictionary as the one the others are checked against. merge_swapped_contigs.vcf declares the
contigs in the other order, vcf_one_sample.vcf has other samples, and vcf_sorted_samples.vcf
is out of order, which the merge refuses only when it goes backwards. COMMENT keeps only the
first comment (addMetaDataLine refuses a second line under one key). A `.list` INPUT is not
a value: the paths inside it are the container's, and the port runs on the host. OUTPUT is a
.vcf: BCF writing is not in htsjdk-rs, and a .vcf.gz would be another file to compare.
INPUT and COMMENT are whole lists ($lists). gather_1.vcf and gather_2.vcf are consecutive
stretches, given in order, reversed (refused unless REORDER_INPUT_BY_FIRST_VARIANT puts them
back) and around gather_empty.vcf, which has no first record and sorts last when reordered.
gather_overlap.vcf starts after gather_1 starts and before it ends, which only the gather's own
check refuses; gather_2_swapped.vcf has the samples in the other column order, refused beside
gather_1 and accepted alone (its genotypes are re-encoded in that order, where gather_1's are
copied); merge_swapped_contigs.vcf has another dictionary (an AssertionError, which escapes the
tool's catch); merge_b_no_contigs.vcf has none, refused before the catch when indexing and by
a NullPointerException inside it when not. COMMENT keeps only the first comment. OUTPUT is a
.vcf: the block-copying gather needs a .vcf.gz output and every input compressed, and a
.list INPUT names container paths the host port cannot open.
Both outputs are compared (the manifest's output_name names the two). split_types.vcf holds
every VariantContext type, its first odd one MIXED; vcf_sorted_samples.vcf's one odd record
is a symbolic deletion, and vcf_unsorted_samples.vcf is the same records with genotypes that
are re-encoded rather than copied; so STRICT decides between two refusals and two splits. gather_1.vcf (copied) and merge_b.vcf (re-encoded) hold SNPs and indels only, which STRICT accepts.
vcf_no_contigs.vcf is indexable only through SEQUENCE_DICTIONARY, which is read through
SamReaderFactory, so it is a .dict; other.dict disagrees with the VCFs and is accepted,
since it only feeds the index. vcf_sites_only.vcf has no samples. The outputs are .vcf:
BCF writing is not in htsjdk-rs.
INPUT is variants.vcf, which has its .idx, gather_1.vcf.gz, which has its .tbi,
unsorted_indexed.vcf, whose records are out of coordinate order beside a borrowed .idx (the
reader only finds and loads it), so REQUIRE_INDEX lets them through to the tabix index of a
compressed output, which refuses them; and two files with no index, which REQUIRE_INDEX
refuses: vcf_no_contigs.vcf (which CREATE_INDEX refuses) and gather_1.vcf, gather_1.vcf.gz's
own text. OUTPUT is a .vcf, a .vcf.gz (compared decompressed) and a name the writer builder
cannot place; both output names are compared. BCF is not a value on either side: htsjdk-rs
has no BCF codec, so neither a .bcf input nor a .bcf output is ported.
INPUT is fix_missing.vcf, whose records use a FILTER, INFO keys and FORMAT keys its header
does not define (at most one undefined INFO key per record, so which one the writer names
first never depends on a HashMap's order), the same under the other column order (its
genotypes are decoded, so their FORMAT keys are checked when written), vcf_sorted_samples.vcf,
whose header is complete, and vcf_no_contigs.vcf, which the always-indexing writer refuses.
HEADER is `null` (the header is rebuilt from the records), fix_header.vcf (complete),
fix_header_swapped.vcf (the same samples in the other column order, which
ENFORCE_SAME_SAMPLES lets through) and vcf_one_sample.vcf (one sample, refused unless
ENFORCE_SAME_SAMPLES is false, and then missing the definitions). CHECK_FIRST_N_RECORDS is
the default and 1, which scans one record, so a later undefined key reaches the writer, and
which beside a HEADER is the tool's own command-line refusal. OUTPUT is a .vcf: BCF writing
is not in htsjdk-rs.
The locus walk reads every base of the reference, so the inputs are the coordinate-sorted BAMs,
indexed (small.bam, adapters_coordinate.bam) and not (tiled.bam, small.sam): with INTERVALS the
indexed ones are queried and the others scanned, and the two disagree about unmapped reads placed
at their mate. adapters_coordinate.bam is the only input on which PCT_EXC_ADAPTER is not zero;
queryname.bam is the iterator's refusal, kept once.
INTERVALS null walks the whole genome; targets_mixed.interval_list overlaps itself and is uniqued.
The two quality floors move reads and bases between the PCT_EXC_ columns. COVERAGE_CAP=5 is below
this corpus's deepest loci, so it caps and its LOCUS_ACCUMULATION_CAP=1 is raised to it, which then
caps what the iterator accumulates. STOP_AFTER=1000 ends the walk mid-contig, where the exclusion
counters count what the iterator had already pulled. READ_LENGTH=0 sizes the fast collector's
counters to nothing, which it refuses; the slow one never reads it. SAMPLE_SIZE moves
HET_SNP_SENSITIVITY, a Monte-Carlo estimate.
THEORETICAL_SENSITIVITY_OUTPUT and ALLELE_FRACTION are left out: they write a second file this
harness does not compare, and the port refuses that argument rather than writing it.
CollectWgsMetrics' domain (see its $why), around this tool's own defaults: no mapping-quality
floor, a base-quality floor of 3, COVERAGE_CAP 100000 and LOCUS_ACCUMULATION_CAP 200000. The
default cap is kept although every row holding it writes a histogram of 100001 bins: it is the
tool's default and the HET_SNP_SENSITIVITY estimate then samples a thousand and one depths.
CollectWgsMetrics' domain (see its $why), minus USE_FAST_ALGORITHM=true (see the constraint).
READ_LENGTH is held: only the fast collector reads it, and this tool never builds one.
CHART_OUTPUT is held: the chart is R's rendering of the metrics file and is not compared.
Inputs need no sort order here (the collector reads records, not loci), so queryname.bam is an
ordinary input; adapters_coordinate.bam is the one with mapping-quality-zero adapter reads.
BAIT_INTERVALS and TARGET_INTERVALS are lists: baits.interval_list overhangs two targets, misses
the third and adds a bait over nothing, so ON_/NEAR_/OFF_BAIT_BASES all move; the two-file value
is uniqued across files and names the bait set 'baits.targets_mixed'. targets_mixed overlaps
itself, so ZERO_CVG_TARGETS_PCT divides by its four raw intervals, not its three uniqued ones.
METRIC_ACCUMULATION_LEVEL is appended to ALL_READS, and the depth histograms are the collector's
rather than the unit's, so READ_GROUP ends in the reference's own consistency exception; it is
kept once. REFERENCE_SEQUENCE null leaves AT_ and GC_DROPOUT at zero. COVERAGE_CAP=2 and
SAMPLE_SIZE move HET_SNP_SENSITIVITY; NEAR_DISTANCE=0 empties the near-bait band.
PER_TARGET_COVERAGE, PER_BASE_COVERAGE and THEORETICAL_SENSITIVITY_OUTPUT write side files this
harness does not compare, and have no fixture; the port refuses them.
CollectHsMetrics' domain (see its $why) with the amplicons in the baits' place: AMPLICON_INTERVALS is
a single file, so there is no two-file value, and the name comes from CUSTOM_AMPLICON_SET_NAME or
the file. The floors vary around this tool's own defaults: mapping quality 1, base quality 0, and
CLIP_OVERLAPPING_READS false.
OUTPUT is a prefix: the tool writes five files under it, and the manifest compares all five,
with and without FILE_EXTENSION, so a row that moves the files is compared on where they went.
original_quals.bam carries OQ on two pairs in three, which is what makes USE_OQ observable;
one_read_group.bam has a single library and sample, so the per-library split and the sample
alias change. INTERVALS and DB_SNP each take null and a file: the mask and the dbSNP skip both
remove bases. The insert-size bounds reach the filter (150 drops the corpus's short inserts,
0 removes the maximum) and the tool's own validation (-1, and a maximum under the minimum).
CONTEXT_SIZE 0 collapses every context to its centre, and CONTEXTS_TO_PRINT of length three is
then refused; CONTEXT_SIZE 2 is left out because its detail files hold 12,288 rows a library.
CONTEXTS_TO_PRINT is a whole set ($lists), whose refusals come out in HashSet order.
The inputs are detail tables MakeFixtures writes through Picard's own beans: artifacts (two
libraries, every context, some counting nothing), artifacts_subset (one library, four
contexts) and artifacts_broken (ACA without its reverse complement TGT). INPUT_BASE names a
pair, PRE_ADAPTER_IN and BAIT_BIAS_IN override either half, and a pair whose libraries or
contexts do not line up is the NullPointerException Picard throws. OUTPUT_BASE and OXOG_OUT
both name a file in the output directory; see the constraint for why they are never both null.
original_quals.bam carries OQ on two pairs in three, which is what makes USE_OQ observable;
one_read_group.bam has a single library and sample. INTERVALS and DB_SNP each take null and a
file. The insert-size bounds reach the filter (0 and 0 remove it, which lets unpaired reads
in) and the tool's own validation (a maximum under the minimum). CONTEXT_SIZE 0 makes the
contexts single bases; AGT fails the middle-base check, or the length check at size 0.
STOP_AFTER 100 ends the walk after a hundred sites of interest.
SUMMARY_OUTPUT is compared beside OUTPUT; the chart is R's and is not. unmapped.bam has no
aligned read, so every unit writes nothing and R fails on the empty summary, which the tool
ignores; one_read_group.bam has one unit per level. SCAN_WINDOW_SIZE 50 and 1500 move every
window and bin, and 1500 is longer than chr2, whose reads then all land in bin 0.
METRIC_ACCUMULATION_LEVEL is a collection appended to its ALL_READS default ($lists), and
null empties it, which leaves no level at all.
rrbs.bam is bisulfite-converted reference sequence (MakeFixtures): the other BAMs are random
bases, which every row's mismatch filter rejects. small.bam is kept as that case, and
queryname.bam as the sort refusal and, under ASSUME_SORTED, the walker's. The prefix is given
with and without its trailing dot, which name the same two files. The thresholds each take a
value that moves the counts; MINIMUM_READ_LENGTH 0 and MAX_MISMATCH_RATE 1.5 are refused, alone
and together in one message, and MINIMUM_READ_LENGTH 60 makes every read short.
SEQUENCE_NAMES and METRIC_ACCUMULATION_LEVEL are collections ($lists).
refflat.txt is the corpus's own annotation (MakeFixtures): two transcripts of one gene that
disagree on a middle exon, a minus-strand gene under the default MINIMUM_LENGTH, a non-coding
gene overlapping two others, one on chr2 and one on a contig the corpus lacks.
RIBOSOMAL_INTERVALS reuses the target lists: targets.interval_list is sorted, and
targets_mixed overlaps itself and is uniqued. RRNA_FRAGMENT_PERCENTAGE 0.3 widens what counts
as ribosomal, and 0.0 is refused without a ribosomal list and makes every paired fragment
ribosomal with one. MINIMUM_LENGTH 100 lets GENE_B into the coverage metrics; END_BIAS_BASES 10
moves the biases. IGNORE_SEQUENCE is a set of one: chr2 drops a quarter of the reads.
Two refusals were measured and are left out because together they took eleven of the first
28 rows: a ribosomal list whose dictionary differs (other.dict: 'Sequence dictionaries differ
in ...') and an IGNORE_SEQUENCE the header lacks (chrX: 'Unrecognized sequence chrX passed as
argument to IGNORE_SEQUENCE'). The port reproduced both on every such row.
REFERENCE_SEQUENCE is optional here and null drops the reference walker, which is what refuses
a queryname input. METRIC_ACCUMULATION_LEVEL appends to its ALL_READS default ($lists), and
null empties it. The chart is R's and is not compared; OUTPUT and CHART_OUTPUT are held in
the output directory.
replicates.bam (MakeFixtures.writeReplicateFixtures) lays duplicate sets of every size and
allele mix over the heterozygous sites of replicates.vcf; it is indexed, as the tool requires.
mate_cigar.bam is the ordinary corpus with MC tags, two libraries and random bases, so its sets
come out in library order and most of them are three-allelic. replicates_two.vcf adds a
second sample with other genotypes, so SAMPLE decides the sites, and null is refused against
it. MINIMUM_GQ 50 admits chr1:1100 (GQ 60), whose third allele then discards it; MINIMUM_MQ 30
admits the set at mapping quality 35; MINIMUM_BQ 10 counts the base at quality 12 instead of
abandoning its set. MINIMUM_BARCODE_BQ 1 makes the barcode with a '#' usable. BARCODE_TAG and
BARCODE_BQ name tags no read carries (BC, BQ), which empties every barcode. MATRIX_OUTPUT is
compared beside OUTPUT, and null writes none.
Measured and then left out, because with the refusal above they took half of the first
18 rows: an unindexed input (small.sam: 'INPUT file must have an index.') and a sample the
one-sample file lacks ('Cannot find sample sampleS in vcf.'). The port matched both.
lift_vcf.chain and liftover.vcf are written together (MakeFixtures.writeLiftoverFixtures): chr1
lifts forward, chr2's first half onto the reverse strand and its second half to a chr3 the
reference lacks, and every record's REF agrees, disagrees or is swapped with ref.fasta where
it lands, so every rejection reason and both strands are reached. liftover_missing.vcf has
its samples out of order (so its genotypes are re-encoded) and a record bound for chr3, which
is an error unless WARN_ON_MISSING_CONTIG. lift.chain is the forward-only chain, against which
the chr2 records mismatch or have no target. LIFTOVER_MIN_MATCH 0.5 lets the deletion across
the chain's end lift partially, which then straddles. TAGS_TO_REVERSE and TAGS_TO_DROP append
to their defaults ($lists) or are emptied by null; DP is a tag that is not a frequency.
OUTPUT and REJECT are both compared.
PROGRAM is a set appended to the default five ($lists): CollectAlignmentSummaryMetrics names
one of them (the default run), CollectQualityYieldMetrics adds a sixth, and the two lists that
begin with null replace the set with programs that need a reference, a refFlat, intervals and
dbSNP; null alone is refused. The domain is restricted to programs this repository runs end
to end as binaries, which is all nine (CollectMultipleMetrics runs each through its port).
METRIC_ACCUMULATION_LEVEL appends to ALL_READS ($lists); its other levels are kept away from
the program sets that hold CollectInsertSizeMetrics, whose port runs ALL_READS alone.
INTERVALS reaches the artifact metrics and is RnaSeqMetrics' ribosomal list; DB_SNP reaches the
artifact metrics; REF_FLAT null is refused where RnaSeqMetrics runs; IGNORE_SEQUENCE chr2 drops
its reads from RnaSeqMetrics. FILE_EXTENSION moves every metrics file, and the manifest
compares all fourteen names under both spellings. queryname.bam is left out: every row with
it is the sort refusal or the reference walker's, which the single-program arrays measure.
INPUT is sort.gff3 (MakeFixtures: five contigs out of order, comments, sequence-regions,
children before parents, values that need escaping), gff_circular.gff3 (a circular region a
feature runs off) and two refusals: a feature outside its sequence-region, and a file with no
feature, which canDecode rejects like a file that is not GFF3. SEQUENCE_DICTIONARY is none
(contigs sort as strings), the corpus's FASTA (its .dict: chr1, chr2) and other.dict (chr1,
chr2, chr3); a contig the dictionary does not name sorts first. OUTPUT's extension decides the
writer: .gff3 is text, .gff3.gz is BGZF, and .txt is refused after the input has been read.
nRecordsInMemory 3 spills to TMP_DIR and merges back, which must not change the order.
VALIDATION_STRINGENCY and CREATE_INDEX are held at their defaults: the tool opens no SAM or
BAM, so neither is read, and varying them only multiplied the refusal rows (16 rows, 2
accepted).
zcall.vcf, zcall.ped, zcall.map and the thresholds are MakeFixtures' (see writeZCallFixtures).
doWork catches every exception, prints it and returns 0, so a refusal is exit 0 with no file
(thresholds with one NA alone, a PED of two lines, a VCF of two samples) or with the records
written before the one that threw (an illegal PED letter at rs5, a MAP without rs3, and
vcf_one_sample.vcf, whose genotypes carry no extended attribute, so the first record throws
and only the header is written). ZCALL_VERSION is written into the header as given.
bfq.bam is MakeFixtures' (see bfqReads): sixteen queryname-sorted unaligned pairs carrying
every filter the writer applies (XN noise on one or both reads, vendor QC, XT whole-read
clipping and adapter positions), no-calls in and out of the seed region, qualities above 63, a
short pair and a name outside the RUN1: prefix. bfq_odd.bam is the same reads, unsorted, with one
pair broken: the paired path refuses it, READS_TO_ALIGN's sort check refuses it, single-end
reads it. Barclay counts an argument given as `null` as set, so of each mutex pair only one can
be varied: FLOWCELL_BARCODE is held at FC1 with LANE 3 or null (the prefix is FC1.3 or
FC1.null), OUTPUT_FILE_PREFIX is left out, and RUN_BARCODE (null or RUN1, which strips
`RUN1:`) stands for READ_NAME_PREFIX. READ_CHUNK_SIZE 10 splits the output into numbered
files; output_name lists the indices 0 to 3 of both reads under both prefixes. BASES_TO_WRITE
is shorter and longer than the reads. VALIDATION_STRINGENCY and CREATE_INDEX are held: the
fixture's records are valid and the tool writes no BAM.
INPUT is the two-element list ($lists), over MakeFixtures' InsertSizeMetrics tables: a file
against itself (equal, exit 0), against ism_b (one double, long, int and enum changed and one
histogram bin) in both orders, since the relative change is measured against the first file,
against ism_c (the rows reordered, which only KEY matches up), ism_d (a column missing, which
only METRICS_NOT_REQUIRED forgives) and ism_e (fewer rows). The verdict is the exit code, 1
for a difference, with OUTPUT written, so the exit code is part of the answer. METRICS_TO_IGNORE
names a compared column or one the file lacks (refused once the files differ);
METRIC_ALLOWABLE_RELATIVE_CHANGE is a tolerance that forgives the 1% change, one that does not
(the comparison is >=), a non-positive one and one with no colon, both refused by
customCommandLineValidation. KEY matches rows by MEDIAN_INSERT_SIZE (a double, printed as 200.0)
or by SAMPLE and READ_GROUP ($lists), which are null on the first row, and StringUtil.join's
toString() on a null is the NullPointerException the tool rethrows. OUTPUT_TABLE is the
differences as a metrics file. VALIDATION_STRINGENCY and CREATE_INDEX are held: the tool reads
no SAM.
mba_unmapped.bam and mba_aligned.bam are MakeFixtures' (see writeMbaFixtures): one template per
case of the merge. mba_aligned_simple.bam drops the paired multi-hits (so EarliestFragment, which
refuses a paired read with more than one hit, can run), carries two @PG lines (so none is
adopted) and is out of queryname order (so the merge throws, sorts the aligned reads and runs
again). VALIDATION_STRINGENCY is LENIENT or SILENT: STRICT refuses the alignment that runs off
chr2 (t07) as the aligned file is read, which is the case the merge exists to clip. JUMP_SIZE
and READ1/READ2_ALIGNED_BAM are left out: Barclay counts an argument given as `null` as set,
and each is mutually exclusive with one that is always given. The program-group arguments are
held absent: ID, VERSION and COMMAND_LINE must come together, which left free made a partial
set (one refusal) most of the array, and tied by constraints left the generator either
uncovered tuples or rows that break the constraints; the aligned file's own @PG is what the
rows adopt. READ1_TRIM and READ2_TRIM are held at 0: a trim is only consistent with an aligned
file whose reads were all trimmed, and on this one every other read becomes an invalid cigar;
t12's aligned read, shorter than its original, takes the same soft-clipping path. The
attribute lists and EXPECTED_ORIENTATIONS are $lists; ATTRIBUTES_TO_REVERSE(_COMPLEMENT)
append to their defaults, so OQ (E2) keeps the default and `null` empties it.
MATCHING_DICTIONARY_TAGS keeps its default, PAIRED_RUN is ignored by the tool and CREATE_INDEX
writes a side file only.
fp_haplotypes.txt is MakeFixtures' (see writeFingerprintFixtures): seven SNPs in five blocks, each with the
reference base as its major allele, which is what asVcf needs of a SNP. The swapped map has the two alleles the
other way round and the split map has every SNP its own block, so the REF, the AF and the phasing each move.
haplotypes.txt is the lift-over corpus's map, whose alleles are not the reference's: asVcf refuses it by naming
the first SNP, and the refusal is kept as a value. OUTPUT is a .vcf because the writer is picked by the
extension.
fp_crosscheck.metrics has two components (A-B-C, where A-C scores low and comes back inside, and D-E-F) and
a pair joined by nothing above the default threshold; fp_crosscheck_ring.metrics is a ring of four whose last
row (1.5) closes it only under a threshold below that, plus a negative edge and a chain. LOD_THRESHOLD
moves rows between clusters, and 0.0 is the default.
fp_a.bam is sample A (one read group) over the seven sites of fp_haplotypes.txt, with eight duplicate-flagged
reads at chr1:100 and a base in nine under the quality floor; fp_b.bam and fp_c.bam are samples B and C. fp_multi.bam is
left out: it holds two samples, and the tool refuses it with 'Expected exactly 1 fingerprint, found 2' whatever else is
given, which would put that one refusal on every row that drew it. OUTPUT is a .vcf. LOCUS_MAX_READS 10 is under the
depth of every site, so the cap cuts every block.
ExtractFingerprint's corpus (see its $why). The default of LOCUS_MAX_READS is 200 here, and the
second value 10 cuts every block.
fp_a.bam and fp_b.bam are samples A and B over the seven sites of fp_haplotypes.txt (see
writeFingerprintFixtures). fp_genotypes.vcf has A, B and C with PL and fp_genotypes_gt.vcf has them as GT alone, so
GENOTYPE_LOD_THRESHOLD and the genotype error have something to act on; fp_genotypes_a.vcf has A only, and both it and
fp_genotypes.vcf are VCFs the tool takes as its INPUT (the second needs OBSERVED_SAMPLE_ALIAS to say which of its
samples). fp_multi.bam is left out: it holds two samples and the tool refuses it by name whatever else is given. OUTPUT
is a prefix for the two metrics files, and is mutually exclusive with each of them (Barclay refuses on the argument
being set), so SUMMARY_OUTPUT and DETAIL_OUTPUT are held absent. The tool's exit code is part of the answer: a run with
nothing to check returns a code of its own with both files written, and each is given a second value. A sample the
genotypes lack is the third kind of exit, and writes nothing but a log line carrying the wall clock, which no second
implementation can reproduce, so the constraints below keep the sample resolvable.
INPUT is a list ($lists): the tool measures each file and each group, so a row with two files has two
of each. fp_a.bam is sample A, fp_multi.bam is A in two libraries and B in a third, and fp_genotypes.vcf has three
samples, so CALCULATE_BY has something to roll up at every level. The haplotype map is given as it is, with its
alleles swapped, and with every site its own block. NUMBER_OF_SAMPLING moves the random trials the LOD is measured
against, and 10 gives fewer of them than the default.
INPUT and SECOND_INPUT are lists ($lists). fp_a.bam and fp_b.bam are two samples, fp_multi.bam is A twice and B
once (so CROSSCHECK_BY gives three different tables), and fp_genotypes.vcf is a VCF with A, B and C, which is a
second input that is not a BAM. MATRIX_OUTPUT is mutually exclusive with SECOND_INPUT (Barclay refuses on the
argument being set, so even null is fatal) and each has one partner, so the side that changes which pairs are compared
is kept and the matrix is held absent; the matrix is measured through CrosscheckReadGroupFingerprints, whose roll-up
writes it to OUTPUT. The files of file names (INPUT_SAMPLE_MAP, INPUT_INDEX_MAP and their kin) hold paths, which the
container and the host spell differently, so they have no fixture. The tool's exit code is part of the answer, with the
table written either way.
The wrapper of CrosscheckFingerprints (see its $why) that rolls up through two booleans of its own. It refuses
CROSSCHECK_BY, MATRIX_OUTPUT and SECOND_INPUT whenever they are given, whatever their value, so each is held absent;
its EXPECT_ALL_READ_GROUPS_TO_MATCH is mutually exclusive with the parent's EXPECT_ALL_GROUPS_TO_MATCH, which is held
absent too. A roll-up sends the table to /dev/null and writes the matrix to OUTPUT.

constraints.why: OUTPUT_BY_READGROUP=true requires OUTPUT to be a DIRECTORY, and this harness compares one output file, so the repository has no directory to give it: every row carrying it is refused with 'When OUTPUT_BY_READGROUP=true and OUTPUT is provided, it must be a directory'. Eight of the first sixteen rows were that one refusal, and they crowded out the arguments the tool actually varies. The refusal is behaviour and is kept, but as one case rather than half the array, exactly as the FLOW_MODE constraint below keeps its own.

Picard 3.4.0 throws on it: 'FLOW_MODE is obsolete. Flow support now provided by CollectQualityYieldMetricsFlow'. Every row carrying it is rejected before the tool runs, which cost eight of CollectQualityYieldMetrics' eleven rows in the first run (decision 0009). The rejection itself is behaviour worth keeping, but once, as its own case, not as half the array.

These collectors require coordinate order, and no value of ASSUME_SORTED makes a queryname input work: false is refused up front ('should be coordinate sorted but the header says the sort order is queryname') and true lets it through until the reference walk fails mid-stream ('Requesting earlier reference sequence: 0 < 1'). This was first declared as two argument-pair clauses and measuring showed that to be the wrong shape: the input itself is invalid for these tools, not a combination of it with something else. The clause is scoped, because the same file is an ordinary input for SortSam or SamToFastq. Both rejection messages are behaviour the port owes and belong in the conformance manifest as their own cases, not as most of a covering array.

The two-sample file is refused as not single-sample before OLD_SAMPLE_NAME is read, so naming an old sample beside it only repeats that refusal. Without this clause the refusals took eight of the first twelve rows and NEW_SAMPLE_NAME's second value never reached an accepted one. The refusal is kept, with OLD_SAMPLE_NAME=null.

This tool always builds the slow collector, and the fast iterator hands it edge records, so every row with USE_FAST_ALGORITHM=true ends in the same ClassCastException at the first covered locus (htsjdk.samtools.util.EdgingRecordAndOffset$StartEdgingRecordAndOffset cannot be cast to SamLocusIterator$RecordAndOffset). Measured unconstrained, that one refusal took eleven of 21 rows and left five accepted. The port reproduces it (it is a branch of wgs_cli/wgs_walk and matched on every such row of the unconstrained array); it is kept out of the pairwise array so the rows measure the walk.

With neither, the output defaults to INPUT_BASE + '.oxog_metrics', which is inside the fixture directory: the oracle refuses it as unwritable (the mount is read-only) while the port, on the host, would write into the shared corpus. The refusal it would measure is the harness's mount, not the tool, and the write would corrupt the corpus for every later row.

Contexts of three bases are refused at a context size of nought before the tool runs. AGT keeps that refusal (and the middle-base one) as a case; without this clause the pair took a quarter of the first array's rows, which then measured the validator instead of the counters.

replicates.vcf has one sample, so naming the other is refused before the BAM is read ('When sample is not null, VCF must contain supplied sample. Cannot find sample sampleS in vcf.'). The refusal was measured and matched; as a pair it took a sixth of the array, and the null-sample refusal against replicates_two.vcf keeps the check in the array.

The tool refuses the pair before it reads anything, with a logged error ('CREATE_INDEX=true and DISABLE_SORT=true are mutually exclusive.') and an exit code of one. Measured and matched; unconstrained it was a quarter of the array and hid what DISABLE_SORT does to the order of the output.

OriginalAlleles is declared in the output header only under WRITE_ORIGINAL_POSITION, so a reverse-complemented record written with it and without that header line is refused by the writer ('Key OriginalAlleles found in VariantContext field INFO at chr2:700 but this key isn't defined in the VCFHeader...'), after the sort, or at the record under DISABLE_SORT. Measured and matched on both; the triple is forbidden so the rows measure the lift rather than the writer's check.

exclude.--help: prints usage and exits; the row would measure the argument parser, not the tool
exclude.--version: prints the version and exits, same reason
exclude.--QUIET: suppresses the log on stderr; the compared output is stdout and the output file
exclude.--VERBOSITY: log level on stderr, same reason
exclude.--COMPRESSION_LEVEL: changes the deflate level of a written BAM. Varying it would make the output bytes differ for a reason that is not the tool's logic, and the deflate pin is asserted by its own suite (htsjdk-rs decision 0001)
exclude.--USE_JDK_DEFLATER: pinned true by the oracle contract; varying it would compare zlib output against GKL output and call the difference a divergence
exclude.--USE_JDK_INFLATER: pinned true by the oracle contract, same reason
exclude.--CREATE_MD5_FILE: writes a side file whose content is a hash of the output already compared
exclude.--MAX_RECORDS_IN_RAM: spill threshold; it changes how much is buffered, not what is written, and lowering it on a 400-read corpus changes nothing at all
